title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: fee refunds in full and the bank-error ground
content:
## Policy clause

1. **Full refunds only.** A fee on a Savings & Money Market Accounts account is refunded in full, never in part, as one refund entry that names the fee being refunded.
2. **Two grounds.** A refund is made on one of two grounds: bank error, or courtesy waiver.
3. **Bank error.** A bank-error refund applies when the fee was assessed contrary to the savings charter, for example:
   - an excess withdrawal fee on a branch or ATM withdrawal;
   - an excess withdrawal fee on a withdrawal within the free allowance;
   - an excess withdrawal fee beyond the tier's most excess withdrawal fees per cycle;
   - a monthly maintenance fee in a cycle in which a waiver was met.

   A bank-error refund has no time limit and does not count toward the courtesy limit.
4. **Courtesy waiver.** A courtesy refund of a correctly assessed fee is allowed only when every courtesy gate holds.
5. **Once only.** A fee can be refunded at most once.

## Basis of decision

- **Authority.** Whether a fee was assessed contrary to the charter is judged from the account's records (the withdrawal's channel, its position among the cycle's counted withdrawals, the fees already posted in the cycle, the waiver facts of the cycle), not from the customer's account of events.
- **Object correlation.** The refund names one specific fee; the once-only limit is tested on that fee.

## Ground comparison

| Question | Bank error | Courtesy waiver |
|---|---|---|
| Was the fee assessed correctly? | no, it was contrary to the charter | yes |
| Time limit | none | subject to the courtesy gates |
| Counts toward the courtesy limit | no | subject to the courtesy gates |
| Amount | the fee in full | the fee in full |

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- An excess withdrawal fee was attached to an ATM withdrawal posted eight months ago. ATM withdrawals never count, so the fee was contrary to the charter; it is refunded in full on the bank-error ground, and its age does not matter because a bank-error refund has no time limit.
- A maintenance fee posted for a cycle in which the account's lowest end-of-day balance met the tier's minimum daily balance waiver. The fee was contrary to the charter and is refunded in full on the bank-error ground.
- A fee that has already been refunded once is presented again for refund. It cannot be refunded a second time on either ground.

## Points of judgement

**Can half of a fee be refunded?** No; refunds are always of the fee in full.

**Does a bank-error refund use up one of the customer's courtesy refunds?** No; it does not count toward the courtesy limit.
